summary: This defines a blueprint for a robot pet that remembers its name, battery level, and mood, and can perform a trick on request. It is the starting point that the chapter's unit tests will check.

lines.text: Starts the class, a template from which any number of individual robot pets can be created.
The initializer runs automatically each time a new RobotPet is created, and it collects the three details that describe that pet.
Stores the name on the object itself so the pet keeps it for as long as it exists, rather than losing it when the initializer ends.
Records the battery level as an attribute, which is the kind of value a unit test can later inspect or expect to change.
Records the pet's mood, completing the object's state.
Defines a behaviour belonging to every RobotPet; `self` gives the method access to that particular pet's attributes.

lines.code: return f"{self.name} performs a generic trick!"
lines.text: Returns the sentence instead of printing it, which is exactly what makes the method testable: a test can compare the returned string against the expected text.
